messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED @oncall (sev2) - streaming-tail-latency spike in eu-west-1. p95 ~980ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~2.8s. Several SSE clients reporting chunk gaps. Auto-mitigation triggered: route fallback enabled.

maria: seeing same in grafana. tail_latency_streaming_eu p99 jump at 2026-03-15T08:03:00Z. client_backpressure metric spiked for streaming-proxy pool 3.

kevin: confirmed. proxy logs show repeated 504s from upstream model pool and "write timeout" lines. attaching quick log snippet.

kevin: ```
streaming-proxy-3 | 2026-03-15T08:03:12Z WARN write timeout to client id=ab12 route=/v1/stream
streaming-proxy-3 | 2026-03-15T08:03:13Z ERROR upstream request timeout model-pool-7 id=mp-77 status=504
streaming-proxy-3 | 2026-03:08Z INFO queue_depth=42 backlog_ms=2200
```

jen: customer-impact: a handful of customers on EU realtime plan reported stalls and reconnects. CS is triaging. no data-loss, clients eventually reconnect but UX is degraded.

maria: immediate hypothesis: slow consumers + our proxy keepalive/flush thresholds causing chunk aggregation and spikes. also saw many clients stuck at chunk_size ~64KB and not ACKing.

eng-runtime: rolling a quick config change to reduce proxy write buffer and lower keepalive to 10s on the affected pool. will also flip route to fallback-model-small for non-critical tenants to reduce load.

jen: @customer-success I sent note to impacted customers w/ ETA 30m. asking for any reproducer payloads.

kevin: running a quick curl test against streaming proxy: `curl -v --no-buffer https://eu.streaming.redwood/realtime/stream` shows chunk gaps of ~3s.

maria: running k8s snapshot: `kubectl -n prod logs streaming-proxy-3 --since=5m | grep write timeout | wc -l` => 46. Also `kubectl top pod streaming-proxy-3` -> CPU steady, but network rx queue backlog high.

sre-lead: ack. immediate mitigation steps: 1) enable proxy aggressive flush and reduce buffer_size to 16KB, 2) scale streaming-proxy pool by +3 replicas, 3) add short-term circuit-break to fallback route for overloaded model-pool-7. Can we autopush these?

eng-runtime: i'm on it. pushing config via ops-runbook:```
opsctl proxy update --pool eu-west-1 --buffer-size 16KB --keepalive 10s --flush-immediate true
opsctl cluster scale --deployment streaming-proxy --replicas +3 --region eu-west-1
opsctl route set-fallback --model-pool mp-77 --fallback mp-77-small --threshold 30%
```

kevin: after applying buffer/flush change, i see chunk frequency improve within 90s. p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 820ms. p99 trending down but still ~1.4s.

incident-bot: ACTIONS: mitigation_applied by eng-runtime at 2026-03-15T08:07:30Z. paging suppressed.

customer-success: got initial customer confirmation: "latency improved but occasional hiccups remain" — they sent a sample session id for deeper trace.

maria: digging into root cause: two things correlated: (1) model-pool-7 had multiple long-running queries (batching jam), (2) several legacy clients with small reads not honoring chunked flush causing backpressure. metrics: model-pool-7 avg inference_ms increased from 120 -> 420 during spike.

jen: tagging this as SLO breach p99 > 2s for 7m window. filing incident report.

eng-runtime: followups planned: - long-term: tune batching kernel selection for seq-lens, add backpressure signal from proxies to model pools, better circuit breaker tuning. - near-term: set per-tenant throttles for realtime plan and improve observability on chunking intervals.

sre-lead: handing off to next oncall in 25m. @kevin please prepare a short playbook snippet for runbook: what we did, rollback steps, thresholds to alert.

kevin: will add to runbook now. quick notes: rollback = opsctl proxy update --pool eu-west-1 --buffer-size 64KB --keepalive 30s --flush-immediate false; alert thresholds p99_streaming > 1.5s for 5m -> page.

maria: also adding a kpi card to console to show chunk_gap_histogram by region and client_flags for "legacy-chunking" so we can correlate clients causing backpressure.

incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated (partial). severity -> SEV2 -> monitoring for recurrence.

jen: final note for handoff: customers impacted: 4 tenants with realtime sessions, CS notified, follow-up call scheduled in 1h to explain root cause and compensations if needed.

sre-lead: thanks team. postmortem owners: eng-runtime (root cause + technical fix) and customer-success (customer comms). I'll open the postmortem doc and link traces. :white_check_mark:

kevin: uploading perf traces and log dump to the incident doc now.

maria: leaving a final watch for 30m then handing over. thanks. :coffee:
